relations.evidence: śrīmallāḍa ṣāna vinodāya śrīkalyāṇa malla mahākavi viracite

notes: No scribe, commissioner, owner or king is named for this copy; the scribal colophon (fol. 63r7-8) only gives the date and 'saṃpurṇa likhitaṃ'. The two persons listed belong to the author's colophon of the Anaṅgaraṅga itself: Kalyāṇamalla composed it for the amusement (vinodāya) of Lāḍ Khān (śrīmal-Lāḍa-ṣāna, i.e. Lāḍakhāna, son of Ahmad Khan Lodi); Lāḍ Khān is the patron of the original work, not of this manuscript, and is included only so he can be filtered out. Era: year 1005 cannot be VS or ŚS for a Nepali-language commentary in Devanagari; NS 1005 = c. 1885 CE is the only plausible reading, unless the figure is corrupt for VS 19xx. 'ro' after 'śudi 9' is probably the beginning of the weekday (roja/roj) which is lost in the lacuna.
